executive_summary: SD-LEO-INFRA-VENTURE-QUALITY-CAPA-001-D runs the two graduation-track pilots from the chairman-ratified Venture Quality Review Programme (ratification 0afc86e4, D5 sequencing) and ships one preventive gauge. Re-verification against current main and live DB (per this SD's own instruction to re-grep every named file/symbol at claim time, an adversarial RISK sub-agent pass, and a VALIDATION sub-agent pass that itself caught an error in the LEAD worker's own earlier probe methodology) corrected the SD's own text on FOUR points: (1) of the two named experience-review migrations, only 'venture_experience_review_runs' is unapplied live (confirmed via a live PGRST205 'table not found' probe); 'venture_quality_findings_experience_categories' (the CHECK-constraint widen for usability/accessibility/journey_coherence) was INITIALLY misjudged as already-applied from an incomplete-row insert probe that (invalidly) inferred a CHECK pass from a NOT NULL failure on an unrelated column -- a corrected, fully-NOT-NULL-satisfying probe proves it was NEVER applied, and that the live constraint instead reflects sibling CAPA-001-A's unmerged accessibility/performance/responsive widen (commit aa3ca9abd10) -- FR-1 now writes one new UNION-valued migration instead of re-running 20260828 verbatim, which would have regressed -A's categories; (2) the 'design-fidelity gate' the SD asks to 'register' has no producer to read from yet -- lib/eva/qa/stitch-wireframe-qa.js's scoreWireframeFidelity() is fully built and unit-tested but has ZERO production call sites (grep-confirmed: only its own test files reference it), so simply adding a CANDIDATE_GATE_STRINGS entry would create a printed discriminator that never accumulates real observation data; and (3) the scorer's actual input is NOT blueprint_wireframes+wireframe_screens as its own file-header comment claims -- getExportedScreens() reads artifact_type='stitch_design_export' (verified by reading the function body directly), and a live fleet-wide query confirms ZERO ventures, AltifyAI included, have ever produced that artifact. Building the missing Stitch-export producer is a separate, larger, out-of-scope problem (C3.2 asks only to register the reader, not build a new producer) -- so this PRD invokes the scorer against AltifyAI honestly and accepts status='no_screens' as a valid, informational outcome (consistent with ratification 4730357d: 'an honest AltifyAI kill can still represent a successful factory test'), while still wiring the verifier + observe-only gate string so a real signal appears automatically for any future venture that does produce a stitch_design_export artifact. AltifyAI's current_lifecycle_stage is 24 (confirmed live) -- past Stage 20 -- so the experience review runs via the existing out-of-band annex path (docs/reference/experience-review-out-of-band-annex-runbook.md), never the in-traversal path, and never touches Stage-20/23 gating. All new signals land in gates.exit_observe only, never gates.exit (binding) -- matching the SD's explicit exclusion of making either pilot binding; stage 15's current metadata is exactly {metrics, stage_timeout_ms} with no gates key at all (confirmed live), so the migration MUST jsonb_set-merge in the new key, never overwrite metadata wholesale. X3's hourly probe reuses the existing gauge-runner.mjs / GAUGE_REGISTRY / lib/governance/*-guard.js pattern already shipped for the wind-down-recurrence gauge (rather than inventing a parallel mechanism), redesigned per-venture and active-only after a live check found 56 ventures at stage>=20 split across {active, cancelled} -- a global existence check would false-clear on one covered venture while an uncovered active venture goes unnoticed, and would false-alarm on cancelled test fixtures. A RISK sub-agent pass also flagged CAPA-001-A (active/EXEC, commit aa3ca9abd10) is concurrently touching lib/eva/quality-findings/finding-shape.js and a venture_quality_findings CHECK migration -- no file overlap with this SD's touched files, but the same AltifyAI venture_quality_findings rows may see concurrent writes from both SDs; this SD re-verifies the live CHECK constraint shape immediately before FR-2's write rather than assuming point-in-time state stays current.

functional_requirements.title: Apply the outstanding experience-review migration; write a UNION-valued replacement for the second (collision with sibling -A, corrected)
functional_requirements.description: Apply database/migrations/20260828_venture_experience_review_runs.sql via the canonical migration-apply path -- confirmed NOT yet applied against the live DB (a direct select against public.venture_experience_review_runs returns PGRST205 'Could not find the table in the schema cache'). Neither migration lives under database/chairman-gated/, so neither requires a chairman ceremony packet -- this is a normal PLAN/EXEC action. SECOND MIGRATION CORRECTED AFTER TWO ROUNDS OF VERIFICATION: an initial incomplete-row insert probe wrongly suggested database/migrations/20260828_venture_quality_findings_experience_categories.sql (usability/accessibility/journey_coherence) was already live -- that probe was INVALID (it hit a NOT NULL failure on stage_number before Postgres ever evaluated the CHECK constraint, so 'passing' past it proved nothing about the CHECK). A corrected, fully-NOT-NULL-satisfying probe insert shows the LIVE constraint currently accepts only the 10 base categories PLUS accessibility/performance/responsive (from sibling CAPA-001-A's unmerged branch commit aa3ca9abd10, file database/migrations/20260913_venture_quality_findings_capa_baseline_categories.sql) -- 'usability' is REJECTED live (23514 CHECK violation), and 20260828's own file header says it was 'never applied live'. Re-running 20260828 verbatim (DROP+ADD with only the 10-base+usability/accessibility/journey_coherence list) would REGRESS -A's accessibility/performance/responsive support whenever it lands relative to -A's merge. This FR therefore does NOT run 20260828 as authored: it writes ONE NEW additive migration (dated after both 20260828 and -A's 20260913 file) that widens the constraint to the UNION of everything known-needed -- the 10 base categories + accessibility/performance/responsive (-A) + usability/journey_coherence (this SD's C3.1 need) = 15 DISTINCT VALUES TOTAL, not 13 -- a TESTING sub-agent pass caught that '13' is an arithmetic error that happens to equal the ORIGINAL, UNRELATED 20260828 file's own value count (10 base + usability/accessibility/journey_coherence, which OMITS performance/responsive) -- an implementer who trusts a count instead of the explicit name list could silently reapply that wrong, narrower file and recreate the exact -A regression this FR exists to prevent. Assert set CONTAINMENT of all 15 named values in tests, never a bare count. Re-verify the live constraint's accepted set immediately before writing this migration (state may have moved again since LEAD-phase verification).
acceptance_criteria: SELECT against public.venture_experience_review_runs succeeds (no PGRST205) after the migration is applied.
A row can be inserted and read back via (venture_id, run_id) uniqueness as the migration defines.

After the new union migration, inserting finding_category IN ('usability','journey_coherence','accessibility','performance','responsive') all pass the CHECK constraint using a complete (all-NOT-NULL-satisfied) test row -- never inferred from an incomplete row. Test asserts CONTAINMENT of all 15 values (10 base + 5 named), not a bare count.
No write is attempted against database/chairman-gated/ or any ceremony-packet mechanism for either migration.

functional_requirements.title: Invoke the existing wireframe-fidelity scorer once against AltifyAI, honestly (the missing producer step)
functional_requirements.description: lib/eva/qa/stitch-wireframe-qa.js exports scoreWireframeFidelity(ventureId, {threshold}) -- built and unit-tested (tests/unit/eva/qa/stitch-wireframe-qa*.test.js) but grep-confirmed to have ZERO non-test call sites anywhere in the codebase. Its getWireframes() reads artifact_type='blueprint_wireframes' (AltifyAI has a current one) but getExportedScreens() reads artifact_type='stitch_design_export' -- confirmed live that ZERO ventures fleet-wide (AltifyAI included) have ever produced this artifact type, so the call is EXPECTED to return {status:'no_screens'} for AltifyAI today. Add a small script (scripts/eva/run-wireframe-fidelity-qa.mjs, mirroring the shape of the existing gather-context.mjs/record-review.mjs CLI pair) that calls scoreWireframeFidelity('50763b6a-1fad-4e1e-b2fc-296a1d66ebf9') once, persists whatever real result comes back (including 'no_screens' -- never fabricate screens or force a pass), and prints the result. Building the missing stitch_design_export producer is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this SD (a separate, larger factory-level gap, not what C3.2 asks for) -- if AltifyAI returns 'no_screens', that absence is itself the documented, honest finding for Solomon's report, per ratification 4730357d.
acceptance_criteria: The script runs to completion without throwing and reports scoreWireframeFidelity's real returned status verbatim (completed, no_screens, no_wireframes, or vision_api_unavailable), whichever is true.

If status='completed', stitch_qa_report artifact for AltifyAI gains a metadata.wireframe_fidelity field. If status is anything else (e.g. 'no_screens'), no stitch_qa_report artifact is fabricated -- absence is recorded as a finding, not papered over.
The run does not modify blueprint_wireframes or wireframe_screens artifacts (read-only against those two).

functional_requirements.title: Wire a design-fidelity observe-only exit gate at Stage 15 and register it in bind-criterion-checker
functional_requirements.description: Three-part wiring, all observe-only (never binding): (a) add verifyDesignFidelityReviewed to lib/eva/lifecycle/exit-gate-verifiers.js's GATE_VERIFIERS (match string e.g. 'design fidelity reviewed'), reading the venture's current stitch_qa_report artifact and returning satisfied=true only when metadata.wireframe_fidelity.status==='completed' AND aggregate.fail_count===0, fail-closed (missing artifact, or status!=='completed' e.g. 'no_screens' -> satisfied:false with a reason), matching the existing verifier conventions in that file; (b) add the gate string 'design fidelity reviewed' to Stage 15's venture_stages.metadata.gates.exit_observe array via an ADDITIVE, MERGE-SAFE migration -- Stage 15's live metadata is confirmed to be EXACTLY {metrics, stage_timeout_ms} with no gates key at all, so the migration MUST use jsonb_set(metadata, '{gates,exit_observe}', ..., true) (or an equivalent read-merge-write), NEVER a blind UPDATE...SET metadata='{...}' that would silently destroy the existing metrics/stage_timeout_ms keys; gates.exit (binding) is never touched or created; (c) add {stage_number: 15, gate_string: 'design fidelity reviewed'} to CANDIDATE_GATE_STRINGS in lib/eva/lifecycle/bind-criterion-checker.js so scripts/eva/check-bind-criteria.mjs starts tracking graduation-readiness (MIN_ROWS=25, MIN_SPAN_HOURS=48, zero MarketLens false-rejects) for this string going forward. This closes the exact producer/reader split named as Root Cause B in ratification 0afc86e4 for this one dimension.
acceptance_criteria: resolveVerifier('design fidelity reviewed') returns the new verifier function.

Stage 15's venture_stages.metadata.gates.exit_observe contains 'design fidelity reviewed' after the migration; gates.exit for stage 15 is unchanged (still absent/unset); metadata.metrics and metadata.stage_timeout_ms are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after the migration (proves the merge, not overwrite).
CANDIDATE_GATE_STRINGS in bind-criterion-checker.js includes {stage_number: 15, gate_string: 'design fidelity reviewed'}.
A unit test proves the verifier is fail-closed when stitch_qa_report is missing OR status is not 'completed' (e.g. 'no_screens'), and satisfied when a completed, zero-fail-count report exists.

functional_requirements.title: Hourly gauge: experience-review coverage for ventures at stage>=20 (X3, preventive)
functional_requirements.description: Reuse the exact gauge-runner.mjs / GAUGE_REGISTRY / lib/governance/*-guard.js pattern already shipped for the 'wind-down-recurrence' gauge (same file family, same hourly cron: .github/workflows/gauge-runner-cron.yml). A live check found 56 ventures at current_lifecycle_stage>=20, statuses split across {active, cancelled} -- so the gauge is PER-VENTURE and ACTIVE-ONLY, not a single global existence check (a global check would false-CLEAR on any one covered venture while an uncovered active venture goes unnoticed, and would false-ALARM by counting cancelled test fixtures). New files: lib/governance/experience-review-coverage-guard.js (pure evaluator over the input {qualifyingVentureIds: string[], coveredVentureIds: Set<string>}, returning an EXPLICIT tri-state {status: 'not_applicable'|'clear'|'alarmed', alarmed: boolean, ...} -- a TESTING sub-agent pass flagged that the existing wind-down-recurrence-guard.js template returns only a binary {alarmed, reason}, which would make 'not_applicable' collapse indistinguishably into 'clear' (both alarmed:false) if copied as-is; this guard MUST carry the extra status discriminator so a caller can tell 'nothing to check yet' apart from 'checked and clean'. status='not_applicable' when qualifyingVentureIds (status='active' AND current_lifecycle_stage>=20) is empty (never alarmed); status='alarmed' when at least one qualifying id has zero venture_experience_review_runs rows; else status='clear'. Matches the 'a guard may decline, never report a number it did not take' convention; the executor throws rather than coercing a non-finite/errored query result to a count, mirroring wind-down-recurrence-check.mjs's own guard against that exact failure mode), scripts/gauges/experience-review-coverage-check.mjs (executor: query ventures where status='active' AND current_lifecycle_stage>=20, query venture_experience_review_runs for those venture_ids, call the pure evaluator, exit 1 if alarmed). Register in GAUGE_REGISTRY (lib/governance/gauge-registry.js) with id 'experience-review-coverage', ownerRole 'solomon' (feedback 3b22d053 names this a Solomon-owned miss), and wire the detectorFn key into gauge-runner.mjs's resolver map (same shape as the existing 'wind-down-recurrence' entry). PREVENTIVE-CLASS PER RATIFICATION 49656c8c / D5: this SD's own completion bar for FR-5 is 'gauge shipped, registered, enabled, picked up by the existing hourly cron' -- the programme-level exit predicate of two consecutive weekly non-alarmed readings belongs to the PARENT SD-LEO-INFRA-VENTURE-QUALITY-CAPA-001's own tracking, not a blocking condition on this child's own LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL.
acceptance_criteria: node scripts/gauges/experience-review-coverage-check.mjs exits 0 or 1 correctly against a live/mocked DB in three cases, each with its own status field (not just alarmed:boolean): zero qualifying (active, stage>=20) ventures -> status='not_applicable', exit 0; all qualifying ventures covered -> status='clear', exit 0; at least one qualifying active venture uncovered -> status='alarmed', exit 1.
The gauge query excludes status='cancelled' ventures from both the qualifying population and the alarm decision.
GAUGE_REGISTRY contains an enabled entry with id 'experience-review-coverage' and a tripWhen predicate reading result.alarmed.
gauge-runner.mjs's resolver map has a matching key so the gauge actually executes on the next hourly cron run (not merely registered-but-unresolved).

risks.risk: Two sibling SDs (this one and CAPA-001-A) each widen the SAME venture_quality_findings_finding_category_check constraint with different, non-union value lists -- whichever migration is applied last silently regresses the other's categories if applied as originally authored
risks.mitigation: FR-1 does not re-run 20260828 verbatim; it writes one new migration with the full union (10 base + -A's accessibility/performance/responsive + this SD's usability/journey_coherence) and re-verifies the live constraint's accepted set immediately before applying, not relying on a point-in-time LEAD-phase snapshot.
